$comment: Unit conversions for reconciliation. Explicit and reviewable. Anything absent from this table is REFUSED, never inferred. A conversion is a claim about what a source means, so every factor names the text that supports it. Months and years are deliberately absent: 'one month' is not a fixed number of days in any issuance here, and guessing would manufacture precision the source does not have.

conversions.basis: A week is seven days. MARADMIN 051/23 para 7.a.(1) states the same entitlement as '12 weeks (84 days)', which confirms the factor is what the issuing authority itself applies to this concept.
A day is twenty-four hours. Used only where a source states a period in hours, as MARADMIN 051/23 para 8.b.(1) does with the 72-hour merge period.

refused.reason: No fixed day count. No issuance in this corpus defines it, and inferring 30 or 31 would manufacture precision.
The one-year forfeiture period in MARADMIN 051/23 para 8.c.(3) is already encoded as 365 days by the source's own arithmetic. Converting elsewhere would invite a leap-year error nobody would catch.
